chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: First trip to Chicago as a boy via the railroad pass
summary: At sixteen Zutty left New Orleans with friends on a railroad work pass, got off at Clinton, Illinois, rode in a coal bin to Chicago, walked through the yards and met Red Ernest's family at 35th and State.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well now, when is it that you make this terrific trip to Chicago? When do you go to Chicago on the train?
Oh that was way before.
We haven't done that you know?
That was before he went in the Navy.
Yes.
Oh you skipped, you skipped that?
Oh yes. I was just a baby.
He must have been around fifteen, sixteen.
Sixteen, that's when I was in Chicago.
Well who did you go with?
Nobody.
Just nobody. Just the Gebbes (Gayness?) boys that owned, their uncle owned an undertaking parlor. GEBBES, Gebbes, yes Just left. ......
Wanted to see Chicago.
Just wanted to see Chicago. Left, Clinton, Illinois, that's where I walked off. Because we were going to work on the railroad. But I wanted to hear Tony Jackson.
Yes but I mean how did you come to leave New Orleans?

Because I was going to go on a MULE ship in front see, and then I changed my mind about that. And they used to send out passes to go work on the railroad. See, and this pass brought us to Clinton, Illinois.
Oh, I see. Yes, yes.
And from Clinton, Illinois that's when I put it down.
Did you actually work on the railroad?
No. I never did.
But you just took the pass?

Yes, I'd taken that trip because I wanted to get to Chicago. And you know how you hear rumours around. 'Well if you get to Clinton, Chicago is not too far.' And that's when I asked this engineer or fireman whoever he was because I was cold back in that iron laying on that steel. And I came up to ask him, could I shovel coal? And I didn't know nothing about that either. And that's when he told me, go sit back in the coal bin until I got to Chicago. And when I got to Chicago I just walked right on through
the yards.
And although they had all these tough detectives....

That's right. That's where they had the toughest railroad detectives in the world. And I went right on through and didn't have, didn't was bothered once. And I went to 35th and State, that's when I met Red Ernest. His brother and I was in the navy together.
Red?
Red Ernest.
Ernest?
Yes.
He wasn't a musician?
Oh no.
No.

No, he was a nice big Knights of Python Cat. That's what he wound up being here in the Imperial Lodge up here on 129th Street. Because I saw him several times. And that's when I wanted to go and have that banana split you know, dirty and crummy and everything.
Well what money had you got then when you got to Chicago? Had you got any money?
Yes, I had a few dollars you know.
Yes. Well just tell about this …….
